items.title: US strikes Iran after Trump slams 'foolish' ceasefire breach
items.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps vows a "swift and decisive" response, according to Iranian state television, claiming it had repelled a US attack on Sirik Island, on the shores of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Why hasn't the global economy completely collapsed?
items.description: An unfortunate side effect of the incompetent and erratic negotiating tactics of the Trump administration is that some of the underlying stories in the global economy can get overlooked.

items.title: Shock results from peptide test reveal 'life-threatening' ingredients
items.description: Doctors warn of an "enormous" risk of overdose after testing of a popular unapproved weight loss peptide reveals the product had double the strength of what was listed on its label.

items.title: The dry heart of Australia is now awash with water
items.description: The myth of an inland sea lured 19th century European explorers into the heart of Australia. But where they found only desert, this year it's awash, with water levels at Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre now the best some locals have ever seen.

items.title: Defence home loan subsidy to change after veterans left worse off
items.description: Critics say the scheme, which offers subsidised home loans, lumps Defence members and veterans with uncompetitive rates.

items.title: Venezuela's quake began with a 'soft shake' and then the lights went out
items.description: As a rare one-two punch of earthquakes hit Venezuela this week, residents in the capital Caracas watched in horror as buildings shook and were sent "pancaking" before their eyes.

items.title: Farewell: 27 things Virginia Trioli learned at the ABC
items.description: After almost 40 years in Australian journalism, 27 of them at the ABC, I am now in possession of enough mistakes to claim a small amount of experience.

items.title: At 80, John Williamson is ready to hang up his guitar
items.description: Now that folk and country music legend John Williamson is 80, he wants to spend less time touring and more time at home eating his own tomatoes.

items.title: One Nation won Farrer. Winning over Farrer is another matter
items.description: Farrer residents decisively voted to change their once-safe seat. They are now putting Pauline Hanson and One Nation to the test.

items.title: Live: Injured Socceroos leave camp, France star bags rapid hat-trick
items.description: France beats Norway 4-1 thanks to an Ousmane Dembele hat-trick to top Group I, while Senegal's 5-0 win over Iraq gives it a strong chance of qualifying from third. Follow live.

items.title: The deadly H5 bird flu is here. These global numbers could be a warning
items.description: The deadly H5 bird flu has finally hit Australia. Here's how other nations have coped with the virus.

items.title: Why fuel price drops won't mean cheaper airfares
items.description: Airlines raised prices for flights in response to high fuel costs but experts say there will be a lag in bringing airfares back down.

items.title: Can the Victorian Liberal Party avoid falling apart again?
items.description: The Victorian Liberal Party is competitive in the polls just months out from the November state election. But will party infighting blunt its winning edge?

items.title: This boat smuggled tonnes of drugs into a remote Qld boat ramp
items.description: Inside the journey of how the drugs from Australia's biggest seizure reached our shores.

items.title: Singles ditch apps and head to the bush in search of love
items.description: Forget swiping right, singles are being urged to head to the bush in their search for real-life romance.

items.title: CJ wowed audiences on The Piano. Now he's sharing a stage with the MSO
items.description: The Piano taught CJ Jones about friendship and perseverance. He’s now set for his debut on the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra concert stage at the ABC Classic 100 in Concert.

items.title: When you buy merch at a gig, bands aren't making as much as you'd think
items.description: Three years after a defining flashpoint in the dispute over merchandise cuts, venues and artists are still at an impasse.

items.title: While teaching about pancreatic cancer, John realised he ticked every box
items.description: Clinical worker John McNeur didn't realise he was unwell until he was delivering a health workshop on pancreatic cancer in the remote Northern Territory — and he began ticking all of the boxes. Now he's on a mission to raise awareness.

items.title: Help to get Indigenous groups 'out of poverty trap' absent in NSW budget
items.description: There have been three state budgets since the failed Voice referendum in October 2023, and this year marked the fourth for the Minns Labor government.

items.title: 'You can hear them': Thousands of dung beetles exchanged via post
items.description: While some dung beetles rest, others get to work, and farmers are making trades.

items.title: Small plane crashes into Beijing's tallest building
items.description: Two bystanders have said an aircraft about the size of a car has crashed into Beijing's CITIC Tower.

items.title: Should dementia patients be able to choose to die?
items.description: Families and dementia patients say they should be able to die on their own terms, so why isn't dementia treated like other incurable diseases? What would it take to change Voluntary Assisted Dying laws?

items.title: 'It's an honour': Australian drawn to face Serena in Wimbledon opener
items.description: Australia's Maya Joint will take centre stage at Wimbledon after she was drawn to face Serena Williams in the opening round.

items.title: Football helps refugees forge connections in Australia
items.description: On a crisp winter's evening at Fairfield in Western Sydney, a common passion warms a group of footballers braving the night air.

items.title: Art 'like medicine' for accountant turned artist after brain injury
items.description: After undergoing brain surgery, Cheryl Blacklock can no longer process numbers quickly and has instead found a new life through art, painting faces that appear as visions in her mind.
